text:
elaine: quick sync — following the cache-throttle outage this morning i sketched a tiny PRD update + runbook additions. we need to lock these before next deploy window. doc: https://internal.redwood/collab/cache-throttle-prd (edit link)

elaine: TL;DR proposed requirements to add to PRD:
- automated model fallback to a smaller/quantized variant when per-tenant kv cache miss rate > 30% for 2m
- soft per-tenant prefix KV cache limit + telemetry (opt-in enforcement in beta)
- queue circuit-breaker: reject with 429 once request queue > 75th percentile * 3 for 1m
- explicit runbook steps + playbook snippets for SRE on capacity surge

devon: can you paste acceptance criteria here? ops needs concrete SLO impacts to sign off.

elaine: acceptance criteria (draft):
- fallback correctness: 99% of calls after fallback return within 2x baseline p95 latency and pass existing parsing/eval tests
- safe rollback: ability to disable fallback per-customer within 30s via console toggles + API
- observability: dashboards showing per-tenant cache size, miss rate, fallback events, and queue length; alert when fallback events > 5/min for same tenant
- runbook: step-by-step <5min mitigation for surge, including exact queries to purge local cache and how to force fallback off

sam: runtime notes — fallback needs kernel selection + small-variant loading without blocking main pool. edge cases: streaming sessions where KV cache is partial; we must preserve token continuity or reject streaming gracefully. pseudocode: 
```
if queue_len > QUEUE_THRESHOLD and fallback_candidate_available:
  trigger_fallback_async(request)
elif queue_len > HARD_LIMIT:
  return 429, {"Retry-After": 3}
```

maria: runbook additions from SRE side:
- alert thresholds: queue_len > 1000 OR per-tenant miss_rate > 0.35 for 2m -> PagerDuty P1
- playbook quick-actions: 1) scale dedicated pool (if available) 2) enable per-tenant fallback 3) route affected traffic to regional standby
- post-incident telemetry to attach to PRD: sample logs, example tenant id, correlation ids

chris: product/UX: when we return 429 or fallback, surface customer-friendly reason codes and a docs link. example header: `X-Redwood-Reason: cache-throttle; X-Redwood-Action: fallback` and body: {"error": "temporary_throttle", "retry_after": 3, "runbook": "https://internal.redwood/docs/cache-throttle"}

devon: negotiate scope: the per-tenant hard global prefix limit is risky for this cycle — we can do soft-limit + telemetry + beta flag. implement enforcement in next cycle after a small closed beta (2 customers).

elaine: agreed. update: change requirement to soft-limit + telemetry + admin flag for enforcement. acceptance criteria updated accordingly.

ops-bot: RFC created: #2186 "prd: cache-throttle guardrails and runbook" assigned to devon, sam, maria. link: https://internal.redwood/rfcs/2186

elaine: owners: devon -> runtime changes and fallback, sam -> model variant fast-load, maria -> runbook + alerts, chris -> error surface & docs. i'll convert this thread into the PRD change list and ping eng leads. please add any edge cases i missed. :white_check_mark:

devon: one more edge: multi-tenant k/v eviction could evict hot prefixes for other requests — add requirement: eviction policy must not prefer tenant-level fairness violations; scoreboard telemetry required.

maria: noted. will add test play to simulate tenant skew during chaos run.

chris: i'll draft the customer-facing status copy and error UX in the docs repo.

elaine: thanks all. i'll open the PRD patch by EOD and tag owners. if no objections by noon tomorrow we cut the changes into the release train. :rocket:
